items.title: Web Scraping with Python for Beginners: Web Page to Spreadsheet (requests + BeautifulSoup)
items.description:
Write your first web scraper in Python: download a page with requests, find every product with BeautifulSoup and CSS selectors, loop over all the pages and save the result to a CSV you can open in Excel. Includes the three errors every beginner hits (NoneType, 404 and data loaded by JavaScript), and every output on screen is the real result of the code shown, run against a practice shop on my own computer.

Install
pip install requests beautifulsoup4 pandas

scraper.py (full script)
import time
import requests
import pandas as pd
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
from urllib.parse import urljoin

BASE = "http://localhost:8000/catalog/page-{}.html"
rows = []

for page in range(1, 4):
    url = BASE.format(page)
    response = requests.get(url, timeout=10)
    response.raise_for_status()
    soup = BeautifulSoup(response.text, "html.parser")

    for book in soup.select("article.book"):
        link = book.select_one(".title a")
        rows.append({
            "title": link.get_text(strip=True),
            "author": book.select_one(".author").get_text(strip=True).removeprefix("by "),
            "price": float(book.select_one(".price").get_text(strip=True).lstrip("$")),
            "stars": int(book.select_one(".rating")["data-stars"]),
            "in_stock": book.select_one(".stock").get_text(strip=True) == "In stock",
            "link": urljoin(url, link["href"]),
        })
    print(f"Page {page}: {len(rows)} books so far")
    time.sleep(1)

df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
df.to_csv("books.csv", index=False)
print("Saved", len(df), "books to books.csv")

The three mistakes
1. AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get_text': the selector found nothing (typo in the class name). Copy the class name from right-click, Inspect.
2. A page that doesn't exist returns status 404 without stopping your script. Add response.raise_for_status().
3. The browser shows data but Python finds nothing: that part is added by JavaScript. Look in the Network tab of the developer tools for the data file (JSON) and request it directly.

Scrape the right way: public pages only, read the site's terms and robots.txt, pause between pages, never collect personal data.

Pro tip: check robots.txt in code
from urllib.robotparser import RobotFileParser
robots = RobotFileParser("https://example.com/robots.txt")
robots.read()
print(robots.can_fetch("*", "https://example.com/some-page"))
